slides.text: As a forensic audio analyst, I listen to the last moments of people’s lives. 911 calls, black boxes, accidental voicemails. I filter out the static to find the truth. But the recording from the Blackwood Manor murders made no sense. Four bodies, no witnesses. The only clue was a pocket recorder found on the patriarch. When I hit play, I didn't hear screams or gunshots. I heard my own voice, whispering a chilling countdown.

'Five, four, three, two, one,' my recorded voice echoed in the sterile lab. I felt a violent chill. I had never been to Blackwood Manor. I didn't even know the victims. I ran the audio through every biometric filter, desperately trying to prove it was a deepfake or a synthetic copy. The software hit a 100 percent match. It was my vocal cords, my breathing patterns. I was listening to myself orchestrate a slaughter.

Panic setting in, I reviewed the file's metadata. The recording wasn't made on the night of the murders. It was time-stamped for tomorrow night. My phone buzzed on the desk. An unknown number. I answered it with trembling hands. 'Did you listen to the tape?' a distorted voice asked. 'Good. Now you know exactly what you have to do at the Mayor's house tomorrow. If you don't follow the script, your daughter dies.'
